ai.description: *Ophisops minor* (Lacertidae) reaches 4–5 cm snout-vent length. It is brown with pale dorsolateral stripes and possesses fused eyelids forming a transparent spectacle.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ophisops minor* is best distinguished by its fused eyelids forming a transparent spectacle, combined with a distinct lack of a visible lower eyelid or movable lid.
ai.habitat: *Ophisops minor* inhabits arid and semi-arid scrublands, grasslands, and sandy plains across the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Lesser Snake-eyed Lacerta is a diurnal forager that actively hunts small arthropods across open, sandy habitats during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ophisops minor* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ophisops minor* is found in the arid and semi-arid regions of northwestern India, specifically across Rajasthan, Gujarat, and parts of Haryana, typically at low elevations.
